beats.narration_text: Five terms. Ollama: the program that serves an open model. Apptainer: a tool that runs containers without root. A Slurm job: your request for a compute node. A harness: the coding agent that sends the requests. And a context window: how much text the model can see at once.

beats.act: I · The Idea And Its Layers
beats.narration_text: Here is the idea. You ask Slurm for a GPU. On that GPU you run an open model. And a coding agent, like Claude Code, sends it requests and runs tools on your files. There is no per-token bill, because the model is yours for as long as the job runs.

beats.act: I · The Idea And Its Layers
beats.narration_text: There are three layers. The model host is Ollama, inside an Apptainer container, on a GPU node that Slurm gave you. The harness is the coding agent: Claude Code, Aider, or Continue. And the transport is whatever joins them: nothing, if they share a machine, or an S S H tunnel.

Bands build bottom to top on the spoken words.

beats.act: I · The Idea And Its Layers

beats.act: I · The Idea And Its Layers
beats.narration_text: Pattern B keeps your editor on your laptop. Only the model's traffic goes to the cluster, through an S S H tunnel to the login node and on to the GPU node. So the model must be reachable from the login node, and that needs a lock in front of it.

beats.narration_text: Advice that circulates about this setup has traps. First, the network. Ollama has no authentication, and its container image listens on every address by default. On a shared cluster that opens the whole interface, including pulling and deleting models, to anyone who can reach the node.

Real mono text only for the two addresses.

beats.narration_text: Inside Apptainer, the image's own setting beats a plain export from your shell. So pass the address with the env flag: bound to localhost, on a random port. That is what the start script does.

beats.narration_text: Second, the address. Claude Code adds slash v one slash messages itself, and the documented examples give a bare host and port. A base address that already ends in slash v one doubles the path, and the request fails. Give it the bare host and port.

beats.narration_text: Third, the model names. Claude Code uses its small model for background tasks, and a separate setting for subagents. Unless you point those at your local model, Ollama can be asked for Claude models it does not have. So the script sets the small, medium and large names, and the subagent model, to one local model.

beats.narration_text: Fourth, context. Ollama sizes its default window by video memory: four thousand tokens under twenty-four gigabytes, thirty-two thousand up to forty-eight. Claude Code's instructions and tool list alone overflow a small window, and the overflow is cut without any error. Ask for sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-six or more.

beats.narration_text: Fifth, the model. A one-and-a-half-billion parameter reasoning model cannot reliably drive an agent loop with dozens of tool definitions. Use a tool-capable coding model, in the range of twenty to a hundred twenty billion parameters.

beats.narration_text: And drop the words zero marginal cost. GPU hours count against fair share, you wait in a queue, and an idle watcher cancels jobs. The accurate claim is no per-token billing. The cost moves to queue time, fair share, and capability.

beats.narration_text: Setup starts with one small environment file. It says where the images, the models and the container cache live. The default is scratch, which is purged on the first Tuesday of every month. Model weights belong in project space, and on one real account scratch was not even writable.

beats.narration_text: Apptainer otherwise caches into a hidden folder in home, and home fills first. So point its cache and temporary folders at your own storage, and pull the images there, on a compute node rather than the login node.

beats.act: IV · Choose A GPU And A Model
beats.narration_text: Two numbers decide whether this works. The model's weights must fit in video memory, and there must be room left for the context window's cache. If either spills over, Ollama pushes layers onto the processor, and generation slows to a crawl.

shot.visual_intent: A tall tank labelled 'video memory'; a block 'weights' sinks in, then a second block 'context cache' stacks on it; both fit with room to spare (a check). Then a bigger cache block overflows the tank top and the spilled part drops onto a small chip labelled 'processor'; a stopwatch beside it slows (hand barely moves) with the word 'crawl'.

beats.narration_text: Models that fit, by download size. The twenty-billion G P T O S S is about fourteen gigabytes. The thirty-billion Qwen three Coder is about nineteen. beats.act: IV · Choose A GPU And A Model
beats.narration_text: The gpu partition gives one GPU per job, so stay inside one card. An H two hundred has about a hundred forty gigabytes, and every model on that list fits with room for a large context. Older cards like V one hundred and T four may fall back to the processor, so check the log, and ask for a newer type.

beats.act: V · Pattern A, On The GPU Node
beats.narration_text: Know the limits. Anthropic's documentation says it does not support pointing Claude Code at non-Claude models, so this works through documented settings but is an unsupported route. Claude Code's built-in web search runs on Anthropic's own backend, and Ollama's layer does not fully support hosted web search. Prompt caching is not supported either.

A road drawn from the chip to a block 'local model' carries a small sign 'documented settings, unsupported route'.

beats.narration_text: Explorer runs a watcher for idle GPUs. Under-use for fifteen minutes earns an email. Under-use for an hour gets the job cancelled. Coding is bursty, with long gaps while you read, so a session you walk away from will be flagged. Never add filler work to keep it alive. Start when you sit down, cancel when you stop, and put long unattended work in batch jobs.

beats.narration_text: Now the shared endpoint for a whole class. beats.narration_text: A service for many people would usually use vLLM, which batches concurrent requests and supports API keys, though its own documentation says not to rely on a key alone. beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. A local model runs inside a GPU job you ask for, with no per-token billing. Pattern A keeps the model and the agent on one node. Pattern B adds a tunnel and a token lock. Bind to localhost, use the bare base address, map every alias, and set the context window high. Pick a tool-capable model that fits video memory with room for the context. Idle GPUs are cancelled, so start when you sit down and cancel when you stop. And a shared endpoint for a class is a question for Research Computing, not a setting.
